text:
sara: Heads up — prod-eu-west ALB started deregistering many targets ~10:20UTC. Symptoms: readiness failures then deregister. Looks correlated with node pool scale events and egress IP rotation. Anyone seen this pattern before?

matt: yup saw it. ALB health -> 502/timeout then `target.deregister` in the logs. Happened right after new nodes joined.

alb-bot: [ALB event] 1967894330 target deregistered: i-0abcdef12345 (target group tg-edge-prod-eu) reason=unhealthy_healthchecks

aj: can you paste the kube events for one of the pods? wondering if readiness probe failed or connection was dropped mid-probe.

jen: grabbing logs now. here's an example from one pod around the time: 
```
2024-03-14T10:20:12Z INFO http: GET /health -> 200 ms=312
2024-03-14T10:20:13Z WARN http: GET /health -> connection reset by peer
2024-03-14T10:20:14Z ERROR kube-probe: readiness check failed: dial tcp 10.42.3.56:8080: i/o timeout
```

kevin: that `connection reset by peer` + dial timeout smells like SNAT port exhaustion or ephemeral IP rotation losing existing conntrack entries. Did we see kube-proxy restarts?

matt: kube-proxy did bounce on a couple of nodes — `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-proxy -o wide` shows restarts on node-4 and node-7 at 10:19:50.

sara: here's the readinessProbe config for the service (unchanged for months):
```
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10
  failureThreshold: 3
```

aj: failureThreshold 3 means ~30s to mark unhealthy. ALB health check interval is 15s with 2 successes threshold — mismatch but not enough to explain immediate deregisters. If kube-proxy restarts, existing conntrack state can drop causing transient timeouts during the probe window.

cloudwatch-bot: [CW Alert] 1967894360 ALB unhealthy host count spike: tg-edge-prod-eu increased by 12 at 10:20UTC.

kevin: ops theory: node autoscaler adds nodes -> cloud provider reassigns egress ENIs (we use custom SNAT pool for edge nodes) -> existing SNAT mappings evaporate or NAT ports exhaust during flurry -> LB healthchecks see timeouts -> targets removed.

jen: confirmed we saw a flurry of outbound flows at 10:19:30 in VPC flow logs from node-7 to 0.0.0.0/0, many retransmits.

sara: mitigation path: 1) increase readiness failureThreshold temporarily to give more grace, 2) increase ALB healthy threshold or use faster grace window on kube side, 3) fix SNAT pool sizing or switch to EIP per node for edge pool. Thoughts?

matt: +1 to adjusting readiness/failureThreshold as short-term. Longer term we should reserve static EIPs for edge nodes or use AWS NAT Gateway per AZ to avoid port churn.

aj: also add a kube-proxy rolling upgrade constraint: don't evict more than 1 kube-proxy pod per AZ during scaleup. That reduces simultaneous conntrack loss.

kevin: I'll open a quick runbook for on-call to follow when ALB spikes happen: check kube-proxy restarts, check SNAT port utilization (`ss -s`, `conntrack -S`), and check ALB event stream.

jen: patched a canary to use `failureThreshold: 6` for the readiness probe in the edge deployment and deployed to staging. will monitor for another scale event.

deploy-bot: deploy started: staging/edge-service @jen (image: edge:2024.03.14-canary) 1967894540

jen: staging looks stable after a simulated scale up. no more immediate deregisters.

sara: great — let's do a short RFC for SNAT pool sizing + long-term plan for per-node EIP and include kube-proxy coordination rules. I'll draft and tag infra-ops. :thumbsup:

kevin: filed infra ticket EDGE-4321 with notes and initial mitigation steps.

matt: thanks everyone, paging on-call if we see this in prod again.

alice (on-call): on it, will run the runbook if CW alerts trigger.
